name: Hananiah
overview: Hananiah was a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of Zerubbabel. His genealogy is recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:19, situating him within the post-exilic community of Judah. No additional notes provide further personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hananiah means 'YHWH is gracious,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:19, highlights a recognition of God's grace but was not specifically given by divine revelation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hananiah as the son of Zerubbabel. Additionally, he is inferred to be the father of Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shecaniah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:21. These relationships place him within a notable lineage in Judah's post-exilic history.
scriptureSignificance: Hananiah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical connection as a son of Zerubbabel, a key figure in the restoration of Judah after the exile. Through his descendants, Hananiah contributes to the continuity of the Davidic line during a critical period of Israel's history. His presence in the biblical record underscores God's ongoing faithfulness to His covenant people through successive generations.
